name: Tasman Peninsula
name_evidence: Wikivoyage region page 'Tasman Peninsula' (en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tasman_Peninsula); Discover Tasmania region page 'Tasman Peninsula' (hobart-and-south/tasman-peninsula); Port Arthur Wikivoyage page.

spots.name: Port Arthur Historic Site
spots.bio: World Heritage convict penitentiary and village ruins at the head of the Tasman Peninsula, the area's main attraction.

spots.name: Three Capes Track
spots.bio: About 48 km multi-day coastal walk from Port Arthur to Fortescue Bay along the peninsula's sea cliffs; passes booked ahead.

spots.name: Cape Hauy
spots.bio: Sea-cliff cape of dolerite spires reached by a day walk from Fortescue Bay, one of the Three Capes Track's highlights.

spots.name: Cape Raoul
spots.bio: Sea-cliff cape in Tasman National Park with a lookout at the end of a 14 km return track of about five hours.

spots.name: Cape Pillar
spots.bio: Sea-cliff cape reached on the middle days of the Three Capes Track, past the Blade rock formation.

spots.name: Tasman National Park
spots.bio: National park protecting the peninsula's sea cliffs, arches, caves and capes, with the Three Capes Track.

spots.name: Tessellated Pavement
spots.bio: Flat shore platform split into block-like sections by the sea, at the northern end of Pirates Bay.

spots.name: Tasman Arch
spots.bio: Natural sea arch on the Tasman Sea coast near Eaglehawk Neck, reached by a short walk from a car park.

spots.name: Devils Kitchen
spots.bio: Sea-carved trench with a cliff-top lookout beside a car park, close to Tasman Arch.

spots.name: Tasman Blowhole
spots.bio: Coastal blowhole on Blowhole Road, a shorter stop than Maingon Blowhole on the same coast.

spots.name: Remarkable Cave
spots.bio: Sea cavern shaped like the outline of Tasmania, seen from a lookout a short walk from Maingon Bay Lookout.

spots.name: Fortescue Bay
spots.bio: Sheltered white-sand bay and campground at the end of the road, popular for swimming and snorkelling.

spots.name: Coal Mines Historic Site
spots.bio: Ruins of an 1833 convict coal mine on the peninsula's north-east, World Heritage listed and free to visit.

spots.name: Tasmanian Devil Unzoo
spots.bio: Wildlife park at Taranna where free-roaming animals, including Tasmanian devils, can be seen and hand-fed.

spots.name: Eaglehawk Neck
spots.bio: Narrow isthmus at the peninsula's gateway, site of the convict dog line, beside several coastal sights.

name: Freycinet
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Freycinet National Park'; Parks Tasmania 'Freycinet National Park'; Discover Tasmania east-coast 'Freycinet National Park' (three counted sources). Named 'Freycinet' (the national park destination); Freycinet National Park itself is the destination and not also a spot.

spots.name: Wineglass Bay Lookout
spots.bio: Lookout over Wineglass Bay on a well-formed walk from the car park, with the classic view of the bay.

spots.name: Wineglass Bay
spots.bio: Crescent of white sand reached by a three-hour walk over the hills from the car park.

spots.name: Mount Amos
spots.bio: Granite summit walk with views over Wineglass Bay, a medium-grade walk of two to four hours return.

spots.name: Cape Tourville Lighthouse
spots.bio: Lighthouse on a boardwalked cliff track at the end of a 6.4 km sealed road, with sweeping coastal views.

spots.name: Friendly Beaches
spots.bio: Long white-sand beaches on the park's north-east side, reached by gravel road and foot tracks.

spots.name: Swansea
spots.bio: Seaside village on Great Oyster Bay facing the Hazards, with a local history museum and the coast's food and wine.

name: Bicheno
name_evidence: Wikivoyage page 'Bicheno'; Discover Tasmania east-coast 'Bicheno' page.

spots.name: The Gulch
spots.bio: Fishing harbour and rocky inlet at Bicheno's south end, with a glass-bottom boat, a seafood cafe and a small aquarium.

spots.name: Bicheno Blowhole
spots.bio: Coastal blowhole reached by a walking track south of the Gulch; unfenced, so take care in rough weather.

spots.name: East Coast Natureworld
spots.bio: Wildlife park on Bicheno's outskirts with daily devil feeding and hand-feeding of free-ranging animals.

spots.name: Douglas-Apsley National Park
spots.bio: National park of dry eucalypt forest, gorges and swimming waterholes on the Douglas and Apsley rivers, west of Bicheno.

spots.name: Apsley Waterhole
spots.bio: Large swimming hole on the Apsley River, a 15-minute return walk from the park's only car park.

spots.name: Cataract Gorge
spots.bio: South Esk river gorge a short walk from the centre, with a suspension bridge, trails, a chairlift and a swimming basin.

spots.name: Queen Victoria Museum & Art Gallery
spots.bio: Tasmania's northern museum and art gallery at Inveresk, with natural science, local history, art, craft and a planetarium.

spots.name: City Park
spots.bio: Victorian-era park in the heart of Launceston, with a Japanese macaque enclosure, a conservatory and old trees.

spots.name: Brickendon Estate
spots.bio: Working farm founded in 1824 at Longford, part of the Australian Convict Sites World Heritage listing, with its original buildings.

spots.name: Woolmers Estate
spots.bio: 1817 Longford estate with a manor house, convict cottages, coach house and the National Rose Garden.

spots.name: Boag's Brewery
spots.bio: Historic Launceston brewery, visited on tours from the Boag's Centre for Beer Lovers at the Tamar Hotel.

spots.name: Duck Reach Power Station
spots.bio: 1895 hydro station at the head of the gorge, reached by a walk of about 1.5 hours return from the Gorge or Trevallyn.

spots.name: Tamar Island Wetlands
spots.bio: Estuary wetland reserve with an interpretation centre, a boardwalk to Tamar Island and bird hides.

spots.name: Tasmania Zoo
spots.bio: Zoo on 900 acres of bushland at Riverside with about 100 native and exotic species.

spots.name: Beaconsfield Mine & Heritage Centre
spots.bio: Heritage centre on the former Beaconsfield gold mine, known for the 2006 rescue of two trapped miners.

spots.name: Low Head Lighthouse
spots.bio: Lighthouse at the mouth of the Tamar, the third built in Australia and its oldest in continuous use.

spots.name: Platypus House
spots.bio: Guided wildlife house at Beauty Point where visitors see platypus and echidnas close up.

spots.name: Seahorse World
spots.bio: Beauty Point aquarium and seahorse breeding farm with tanks of seahorse species.

spots.name: Bass and Flinders Centre
spots.bio: George Town museum with a working replica of the Norfolk, the ship that first sailed around Tasmania, which visitors can board.

spots.name: Brady's Lookout
spots.bio: Lookout over the Tamar River and its vineyards, a short stop on the valley drive north of Launceston.

spots.name: Binalong Bay
spots.bio: Coastal village and white-sand beach at the southern end of the Bay of Fires, good for swimming and kayaking.

spots.name: Eddystone Point Lighthouse
spots.bio: Granite lighthouse at the northern end of the Bay of Fires, with orange-lichen rocks and beaches around the grounds.

spots.name: Mount William National Park
spots.bio: National park of beaches, heath and coastal walks on the northeast tip, known for forester kangaroos and birdlife.

spots.name: Mount William (wukalina) Summit Walk
spots.bio: About 90 minutes return climb to the 216 m summit of wukalina/Mount William, with coastal views toward the Furneaux Group.

spots.name: St Columba Falls
spots.bio: One of Tasmania's tallest waterfalls, reached by a short forest walk from the road near Pyengana.

spots.name: St Helens
spots.bio: Largest town on the northeast coast, on Georges Bay, and the base for the Bay of Fires and Mount William.

spots.name: Pyengana Dairy
spots.bio: Farm dairy at Pyengana where visitors taste aged cheddars and watch cheese-making through a window.

spots.name: Cobler Rocks Walk
spots.bio: Two-hour return walk from banksia heath along fire trails and beach to rocky coastal outlooks.

spots.name: St Helens Mountain Bike Trails
spots.bio: Mountain bike trail network around St Helens, with a ride that finishes at the bay.

name: Stanley
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Stanley (Tasmania)' page and 'Western Tasmania'; The Nut is a named headline attraction. The town is the destination, so it is not also a spot.
notes: Four kept spots within 3 km; the town candidate becomes the destination itself.

spots.name: The Nut
spots.bio: A flat-topped volcanic plug above Stanley, climbed by chairlift or a 4.6 km walk for views over the town and Bass Strait.

spots.name: Highfield Historic Site
spots.bio: A Regency-style colonial homestead on the Stanley coast, with daily self-guided tours.

spots.name: Little Penguin Viewing Area
spots.bio: A viewing area in Stanley where little penguins come ashore at dusk.

spots.name: Godfreys Beach
spots.bio: A beach at Stanley with views of The Nut.
